resources.string: VideoCAT runs on your own server. Type the address you open it at in the browser.
The app only talks to your server. It collects nothing.
That does not look like an address. For example: videocat.example.com
Could not reach %1$s. Check the address and port, and that the phone is on the same network as the server.
%1$s has a certificate the phone does not trust. Use a valid certificate (Let\'s Encrypt, for example) or http:// inside your network.
%1$s answered, but it is not VideoCAT. Check the address and port.
This address is unencrypted (http://) and outside your network: your password would travel in the clear. From outside, use https://.
The server\'s certificate is not valid.
This download cannot be done from the app.
No app on this phone can open this link.
The video could not continue. Close the player and try again.
Ask for my fingerprint to open VideoCAT

Or your face, or the phone\'s PIN, pattern or password. It works as the app\'s password: it asks again when you close the app or lock the phone, so whoever picks up your phone stays out of your catalog.
Set up a screen lock on the phone (Settings › Security) to use this.
Lock again after leaving the app
Confirm it is you to see your catalog.
The phone no longer has a screen lock, so the app lock was turned off.
